cast: The role of Tyler was played by George Lopez until 2006, when he was recast as Benicio del Toro.
spelling_and_continuity: Tyler's electrical panel labels are not correctly spelled.
Loftus has two F's, not one, despite common belief.
production: The Tyler Loftus Show was shot entirely on the real FX soundstage with a live studio audience.
At the 20-minute mark, a boom mic pops into the top of the frame during the scene where Tyler confronts Mikia for his dismissal of Brazilian cheese bread.
Early VFX artist George Lucas got his start working on The Tyler Loftus Show, CGI-ing Tyler Loftus's famous hat after it was mysteriously lost during production.
The famous scene where Tyler screams out loud after kicking a helmet was actually the actor himself breaking his toe, coincidentally after kicking the helmet.
origins: The rivalry between Tyler and Dustin is based on the real-life rivalry between Mozart and Salieri.
Tyler Loftus was not based on a real human being. He was more mytho-historical in nature, scholars believe.
archival_history: Until the year 2025, no copies of The Tyler Loftus Show existed. They were only rediscovered in a storage unit, having been purchased at auction by Kevin Loftus (no relation).
records: The Tyler Loftus Show is the longest-running television series in the history of the planet.
Scientists believe we will run out of Tyler by the year 2097, after which time humanity will be reduced to watching the Dustin Hunt podcast.
reception: The episode where Tyler Loftus reads a book was largely panned by critics for being far too dull to be put on television, described as "visually static."
setting: Movie critics debate whether a city known as Glendale ever really existed, though the large presence of crashed BMWs leads them to believe that this may have inspired the idea of the city of Glendale.
influence: Alejandro Jodorowsky often cited The Tyler Lofftus Show as his primary inspiration for why he began masturbating in public.
history: Until the invention of the cathode ray tube, humanity was forced to make do with Tyler Loftus stage plays, where the cast was often made to perform reruns of the famous Tokyo Trip episode for the jeering crowd.
fandom: Many fans of the show simply like to watch the cooking segment and have no care at all for the narrative of the story.
